change: board 171: the practice exam page advertised an exam shape that does not exist
_context: The live page called itself a FULL LENGTH practice EXAM while carrying 40 MCQ
and 3 free-response questions. The real AP Cybersecurity exam is 60 MCQ and
ONE free-response question, Device Security Analysis. A teacher pacing a class
against this page prepared students for a shape that does not exist.
This is a RELABEL, not a rebuild. Board 176 owns building the 60 + 1 replica.
All 43 questions are carried through untouched, which the suite asserts.
Every mutation below regenerates the sheet under the mutation, so the sheet
under test is the mutated one. That matters: mutating only the generator would
make the byte-identity check fail first, and a suite going red on a DIFFERENT
assertion than the one you meant to test is telling you the rule is hollow.
TWO LAYERS ARE PROVEN SEPARATELY, and the first draft of this manifest proved
only one. The generator refuses to write a sheet that fails its own result
guards, so every mutation aimed at the smoke was caught by the generator first
and the gate correctly reported the targeted guard as still unproven. So the
GENERATOR mutations below edit the generator and expect its refusal, and the
SHEET mutations corrupt the committed CSV directly and expect the smoke's own
assertion, which is the only way to show the smoke would catch a bad sheet no
